critical_requirement: Do not implement strict assignment as Finalize(destination); evaluate RHS; Adjust(destination). RHS must be evaluated exactly once in the original language/compiler order, and must remain readable if it refers to the destination or its enclosing object. A shallow temporary is not sufficient when freeing the destination would free the temporary source referent.

cases.obligation: RHS A remains live and unchanged. Prior B allocation is finalized once; copied B owns independent full content. No move of A.
Self-assignment is safe. Do not free the source referent before preserving value or recognizing the actual compiler self-assignment path.

Evaluate F with original A readable. If RHS evaluation raises, cleanup of already-created temporaries must match actual compiler and must not prematurely finalize A. Value/result construction and later target cleanup must preserve language ordering.

Copy/cleanup order must be qualified against actual compiler; reject unsupported alias schedules rather than granting blanket strict-copy permission. This cannot silently remove an original required use.

Source ownership survives. Whether destination is registered/finalized depends on real compiler initialization/assignment schedule. Partial newly owned parts are reclaimed; shallow source views are not freed.

smallest_source_gap: Retained exp_ch7 describes hook scheduling generically, and exp_ch3 gives function-return elision, but exact relevant normal compiler assignment-expansion path has not been read from a matching pinned exp_ch5 source. No exp_ch5 download or invented ordering correspondence here.
next_before_patch: Inspect exact-ref assignment expansion plus selected actual native expanded schedule when later authorized; add self-assignment, destination-dependent RHS, RHS exception and partial Adjust-failure mutants to the minimal vertical slice.
acceptance_boundary: No new public precondition, cap, explicit snapshot-death rule, suppression or assertion-policy change. This is a soundness obligation on the verifier extension, not an acceptance waiver.
